title: Transport of a composite counit through two inverse comparison squares
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_F,\mathcal D_F$ for $F=E,L$ be categories [def-nagata-category], and let $T_C:\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal C_L$, $T_D:\mathcal D_E\to\mathcal D_L$ be functors (maps preserving identities and composition). For each $F$ supply functors $P_F,G_F:\mathcal C_F\to\mathcal D_F$, $Q_F,H_F:\mathcal D_F\to\mathcal C_F$, and natural isomorphisms $\kappa_F:G_F\xrightarrow{\sim}P_F$, $\rho_F:H_F\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_F$, $u_F:H_FG_F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C_F}$. Here natural means commuting with every morphism of the source category, and all products of functors denote composition, applied right to left. Supply natural isomorphisms
$$a:T_DP_E\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LT_C,\quad d:T_CQ_E\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_LT_D,\quad b:T_DG_E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LT_C,\quad e:T_CH_E\xrightarrow{\sim}H_LT_D$$
satisfying, for $K\in\mathcal C_E$ and $M\in\mathcal D_E$,
$$a_K T_D(\kappa_{E,K})=\kappa_{L,T_CK}b_K,\qquad d_M T_C(\rho_{E,M})=\rho_{L,T_DM}e_M.$$
Put $\lambda_F=\kappa_F^{-1}$, $\nu_F=\rho_F^{-1}$ and
$$v_{F,K}=u_{F,K}H_F(\lambda_{F,K})\nu_{F,P_FK}:Q_FP_FK\longrightarrow K.$$
Then the inverse comparison squares and the expanded counit transport formula are
$$\lambda_{L,T_CK}a_K=b_KT_D(\lambda_{E,K}),\qquad \nu_{L,T_DM}d_M=e_MT_C(\nu_{E,M}),$$
$$v_{L,T_CK}Q_L(a_K)d_{P_EK}=\bigl(u_{L,T_CK}H_L(b_K)e_{G_EK}\bigr)\,T_C\bigl(H_E(\lambda_{E,K})\nu_{E,P_EK}\bigr).$$
The last equality is between arrows $T_CQ_EP_EK\to T_CK$, and is natural in $K$. No relation between $u_E$ and $u_L$, and no adjunction or equivalence axioms beyond the displayed data, is assumed.

source.place: First paragraph, inverse automorphism squares and identity pasting. Agent-formulated categorical extraction of original item Steps 2, 3 and 5: invert both comparison squares, expand the composite counit, and move the comparison factors using naturality.

proof.text:
Use the associativity and identity laws of [def-nagata-category]; throughout juxtaposition means composition right to left. Postcompose the first supplied square by $\lambda_{L,T_CK}$ and precompose it by $T_D(\lambda_{E,K})$. Since $\lambda_L\kappa_L=1$ and $T_D(\kappa_E)T_D(\lambda_E)=T_D(\kappa_E\lambda_E)=1$, this gives
$$\lambda_{L,T_CK}a_K=b_KT_D(\lambda_{E,K}).$$

source.place: Inverse of the first comparison square. Agent-written component calculation for the inverse-square pasting in paragraph 1.

proof.text:
Apply the same cancellation to the second supplied square: postcompose by $
u_{L,T_DM}$ and precompose by $T_C(
u_{E,M})$. The inverse identities and preservation of composition and identities by $T_C$ give
$$
u_{L,T_DM}d_M=e_MT_C(
u_{E,M}).$$
Only the category laws of [def-nagata-category] and the displayed hypotheses are used.

source.place: Inverse of the second comparison square. Agent-written component calculation for the inverse-square pasting in paragraph 1.

proof.text:
The inverse families are natural: for $s:A	o B$ in $\mathcal D_F$, the given equation $ho_{F,B}H_F(s)=Q_F(s)ho_{F,A}$, postcomposed with $
u_{F,B}$ and precomposed with $
u_{F,A}$, gives $H_F(s)
u_{F,A}=
u_{F,B}Q_F(s)$. The identical cancellation for $\kappa_F$ gives $G_F(t)\lambda_{F,A}=\lambda_{F,B}P_F(t)$ for $t:A	o B$ in $\mathcal C_F$. These use the category laws of [def-nagata-category].

source.place: Naturality of inverse comparisons, explicitly by cancellation. Agent-written component calculation for the inverse-square pasting in paragraph 1.

proof.text:
Expand $v_L$ in the left side of the asserted formula. Naturality of $\nu_L$ from Step 3 at $a_K:T_DP_EK\to P_LT_CK$ gives
$$\nu_{L,P_LT_CK}Q_L(a_K)=H_L(a_K)\nu_{L,T_DP_EK}.$$
Thus that left side equals
$$u_{L,T_CK}H_L(\lambda_{L,T_CK}a_K)\nu_{L,T_DP_EK}d_{P_EK}.$$
This is substitution, functoriality of $H_L$ and associativity [def-nagata-category].

source.place: Expansion and the naturality square of the inverse comparison at a_K. Agent-written component calculation for the inverse-square pasting in paragraph 1.

proof.text:
Insert Steps 1 and 2 (with $M=P_EK$) into Step 4. Its expression becomes
$$u_{L,T_CK}H_L(b_K)H_L(T_D(\lambda_{E,K}))e_{P_EK}T_C(\nu_{E,P_EK}).$$
Naturality of the given $e$ at $\lambda_{E,K}:P_EK\to G_EK$ says
$$H_L(T_D(\lambda_{E,K}))e_{P_EK}=e_{G_EK}T_C(H_E(\lambda_{E,K})).$$
Substitute this and combine the last two factors by functoriality of $T_C$. Associativity [def-nagata-category] gives exactly the claimed right side. Each composite starts at $T_CQ_EP_EK$ and ends at $T_CK$; $u_E$ has not been used.

source.place: Pasting the inverse squares, then the naturality square of e at lambda_E. Agent-written component calculation for the inverse-square pasting in paragraph 1.

proof.text:
For $t:K\to K'$ the three equations from Step 3 and the given naturality of $u_F$ are
$$\nu_{F,P_FK'}Q_FP_F(t)=H_FP_F(t)\nu_{F,P_FK},\quad H_F(\lambda_{F,K'})H_FP_F(t)=H_FG_F(t)H_F(\lambda_{F,K}),\quad u_{F,K'}H_FG_F(t)=t u_{F,K}.$$
Multiplication gives $v_{F,K'}Q_FP_F(t)=t v_{F,K}$. Put $w_K=v_{L,T_CK}Q_L(a_K)d_{P_EK}$. Naturality of $a,d$ now gives, by substitution and associativity [def-nagata-category],
$$w_{K'}T_CQ_EP_E(t)=v_{L,T_CK'}Q_L(a_{K'})Q_L(T_DP_E(t))d_{P_EK}=v_{L,T_CK'}Q_L(P_LT_C(t))Q_L(a_K)d_{P_EK}=T_C(t)w_K.$$
The right side proved equal to $w_K$ in Step 5 has the same naturality equation. This proves naturality of the asserted equality without any relation between $u_E$ and $u_L$.
